exposure: Mode of delivery (assisted vaginal delivery vs. non-assisted vaginal delivery or Cesarean section)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (Apgar scores, maximal bilirubin level, length of stay, composite adverse outcomes)
cohort: Singleton neonates born at Hadassah, Hebrew University Medical Center during 2011-2018 (n=82,256)
finding: While SGH is rare after unassisted vaginal or Cesarean delivery, it may still occur in the absence of an attempted assisted vaginal delivery.
